elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase commitment.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 expressly states that “Customer has no minimum purchase ... commitment.”

elements.element: Customer has no minimum volume commitment or restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 expressly disclaims any “volume commitment,” and § 12.3 continues to confirm that Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment.

elements.element: Customer pays only for Services used or ordered.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 states that Customer “will pay only for Services used or ordered during the applicable term.”

elements.element: Any purchase or volume commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: § 2.1 eliminates all minimum purchase and volume commitments, so no commitment extends beyond a current 12-month term.

elements.element: Customer has the right to reduce any purchase or volume commitment.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because Customer has no purchase or volume commitment to reduce.

elements.element: Any reduction may be made on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because § 2.1 imposes no commitment for which a notice-based reduction procedure would be required.

elements.element: Any purchase shortfall is resolved through a true-up.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: without a minimum commitment, no purchase shortfall can arise that requires a true-up mechanism.

elements.element: No penalty applies to a purchase shortfall.
elements.evidence: The take-or-pay obligation and its shortfall exposure have been removed; because there is no minimum commitment, there is no penalized shortfall.

result.reason: The operative redline fully achieves the preferred position by eliminating minimum purchase and volume commitments and limiting payment to Services used or ordered. It therefore also satisfies the fallback as a more Customer-favorable outcome: the fallback mechanisms are unnecessary because no commitment or shortfall exists. The change is confined to the conflicting take-or-pay provision, preserves the unrelated protections in § 12.3, and introduces no contradiction.
